1.pericope_label: Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy, and say thou unto them that prophesy out of their own hearts
debates: Whether the false prophets are among the exiles or in the land
Whether the deceived people share the guilt
Why a message is sent to men past persuading
outliers: Calvin refuses to let the indictment of the impostors excuse their hearers, holding that the people knew the marks by which true prophets were distinguished and blinded themselves in the midst of light
Henry observes that the nation was never imposed on by pretended prophets until it had first rejected and abused the true ones
themes: Men promising a return in three years to people facing seventy
False prophets agreeing among themselves as the true ones do
A testimony left on record against men who will not repent
A building so frail it cannot stand against the weather of heaven

3.pericope_label: Ye have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the Lord
debates: Why the false prophets are called foolish
What point the comparison with foxes turns on
Whether going up into the gaps means teaching or prayer
outliers: Calvin restricts the going up into the gaps to their teaching, against interpreters who refer it to prayer, where Gill and Wesley take in both
Clarke reads the desert as the place a fox hides its prey, making the figure one of prophets who vanish when their predictions fail
themes: Men forging the name of the Omniscient to words of their own devising
Foxes entering a vineyard through the breaches in its wall
A people scattered out of a walled home into open country
A breach in a wall where a brave man is expected to stand

6.pericope_label: And mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies: they shall not be in the assembly of my people
debates: What distinguishes a true promise of mercy from a false one
Why speaking in the name of God is the aggravation of the offence
What the three exclusions of the sentence amount to
outliers: Calvin rejects a subtler reading of the word for assembly, which would make it the experience of God offered to the elect, on the ground that the next clause simply repeats it
Calvin makes the test of a true prophet not the promise of mercy but its being joined to the doctrine of repentance, which the false prophets sever from it
themes: A God divided in half by men who preach only his pardon
A name that is a fount of splendour, used to make darkness
A hand brought forward because a mere threat will not frighten
A register of returning families with certain names left out

10.pericope_label: One built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter
debates: What the untempered mortar is
Whether the false prophets built anything at all
Who was actually seduced by the promise of peace
outliers: Ellicott cites Calvin by name for the sense of the mortar, and traces the word through its other occurrences to show what kind of plaster is meant
Gill restricts the seduced to the people by profession, holding that the truly elect may be deceived in civil matters but not finally in religious ones
themes: A partition wall passed off as a city wall
Mortar of sand and water with the lime left out
Rain that dissolves a wall of unbaked brick until no vestige remains
A proverb that arises the moment a wall comes down

13.pericope_label: Thus will I accomplish my wrath upon the wall, and upon them that have daubed it with untempered morter
debates: Why the same threat is repeated so often
What the uncovering of the foundation means
How men who saw nothing can be said to see visions of peace
outliers: Calvin answers the charge of verbosity by the temper of the hearers, holding that men who took the dreams of impostors for oracles could not be reached by simple language
Calvin concedes the word vision to the false prophets by accommodation, granting them the name of a thing he denies they ever had
themes: A dream taken for an oracle by a people who wanted it
Winds and hail standing at hand to obey an order
Men who claim a whole prophecy vindicated because one detail came true
A wall whose plaster held only as long as the city did

17.pericope_label: Woe to the women that sew pillows to all armholes, and make kerchiefs upon the head of every stature to hunt souls
debates: Why there were prophetesses at all, true or false
What the pillows and kerchiefs were
Whether the sex of these offenders alters the reproof
outliers: Calvin holds that God raised up prophetesses in order to shame the slothfulness of the men, so that the gift itself carried a reproach
Clarke reports an interpreter who takes the second article for a hunting net rather than a head-covering, which suits the clause about hunting souls
themes: A false religion that apes a true one, and so implies it
Cushions laid under the arms of enquirers to counterfeit a trance
A veiled head borrowed from the practice of pagan divination
Ceremonies heaped up by men who have nothing substantial to offer

19.pericope_label: And will ye pollute me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread
debates: What the handfuls of barley show about the offenders
What polluting the name of God amounts to
What the souls are said to be made to do
outliers: Calvin prefers making the souls fly to a paraphrast rendering of perishing, and reads the flying as the lofty speculations by which false teachers hold curious hearers
Calvin restricts the people to be delivered to the elect, holding that many of the stock had by degeneracy forfeited the name
themes: A prophet fee of a few handfuls of cheap grain
Truth turned into a lie, and God thereby reduced to nothing
A name profaned in the one place it was to be peculiarly worshipped
Masks stripped from women whose apparatus had fascinated a people

22.pericope_label: Because with lies ye have made the heart of the righteous sad, whom I have not made sad
debates: How the righteous come to be grieved by lies aimed at the willing
Whether the ending of their visions is reform or exposure
What the deliverance of the people means here
outliers: Calvin denies that the closing promise means any change of mind in the offenders, taking it as a failure of effect rather than of intention
Gill allows that the ceasing of their visions may mean simply that they perished with the city, rather than that they were discredited
themes: Threats scattered so widely that they wound consciences never aimed at
A conscience robbed of confidence in the favour of God
Boys able to see through what had passed for oracles
A judgment shaped in the very form of the sin it answers
